sources.locator: Ch. 12 §a–§b printed pp. 230–233 (PDF pp. 241–243); §d–§f printed pp. 235–238 (PDF pp. 246–249); §g printed pp. 239–241 (PDF pp. 250–252); Appendix A.63–A.66 printed pp. 584–585 (PDF pp. 595–596). Full text of each listed page read in the retrieved 659-page file (SHA-256 f2ddd8fa4d2630…).

contents.name: Ch. 12 §a: every character χ:G→G_m corresponds to the group-like element a(χ) of O(G), one-to-one
Ch. 12 §b + Prop. 12.3: D(M)(R)=Hom(M,R^×) is represented by Spm k[M]; a basis of M decomposes D(M) into copies of G_m and μ_n
Lemma 12.4 with proof: the group-like elements of k[M] are exactly the elements of M, so X(D(M))=M
Examples 12.1–12.2: k[Z]≅O(G_m), k[Z/n]≅O(μ_n), and k[M1×M2]≅k[M1]⊗k[M2] as Hopf algebras
Remark 12.6: e_m notation for the group-algebra basis
Remark 12.5: connectedness and smoothness criteria for D(M) in terms of p-torsion of M
contents.reason: The pair proves the single μ_p non-smoothness instance directly from the local ring k[u]/(u^p); it does not claim or need the general connectedness/smoothness dictionary, which would require the identity-component and reducedness machinery of Ch. 12 not built here.

contents.name: Def. 12.14: tori (become a product of copies of G_m over some field), split tori, and split tori ↔ free Z-modules of finite rank
Example 12.15: X(G_m×G_m)=Z² with characters (t1,t2)↦t1^{m1}t2^{m2}
Def. 12.16: weights of a torus representation
contents.reason: No representation-theoretic content of multiplicative-type groups (weights, weight spaces, gradings) is part of this pair's contract; the split dictionary is used only for characters and group maps, so the weights definition is deliberately not built.

contents.name: Def. 12.17: multiplicative type (diagonalizable over some field); tori are the smooth connected multiplicative groups
Thm. 12.18: equivalences (a)–(d), including 'of multiplicative type iff diagonalizable over k_s', proved via coétale coordinate algebras
Cor. 12.19: diagonalizable over some extension implies diagonalizable over a finite separable extension
Ch. 12 §g: continuity of the Γ-action (open stabilizers) and X*(G)=X(G_{k_s}) with its transport action
Ch. 12 §g construction: D(M)=Spec k[M]^Γ for a f.g. Z-module M with continuous Γ-action
Thm. 12.23 with proof: X* is a contravariant equivalence to f.g. Z-modules with continuous Γ-action, quasi-inverse M↦D(M), via 12.9 and Galois descent A.64/A.66
Ch. 12 §g: the tori are exactly the multiplicative-type groups with X*(G) torsion-free
Cor. 12.24: every multiplicative-type group is an extension of a finite group by a torus
contents.reason: The exact-sequence clause of 12.23 and the torus-by-finite structure theorem are outside this pair's contract; the classification and the torsion-free torus criterion are built, but the extension splitting is deliberately not claimed.

contents.name: Cor. 12.25: Hom(G,H) is unchanged by purely inseparable base change
contents.reason: The pair is field-level classification and does not build inseparability-invariance of Hom functors; importing it would add an unrelated base-change development with no consumer here.

contents.name: Example 12.27: k=R, Γ=Z/2, M=Z with sign action σ(z)=z̄^{-1}, giving the compact group {z:z z̄=1}
Example 12.28: μ_n is of multiplicative type for all n, while (Z/pZ)_k in characteristic p is unipotent and not multiplicative
Notation 12.29: the maximal subtorus H_t=D(M/M_tors)
contents.reason: The largest-subtorus notation presupposes the torus-by-finite structure of 12.24, which this pair does not build; the corollary already isolates the torsion-free case, so no consumer needs H_t.

contents.name: A.64: semilinear Galois descent for K-vector spaces is an equivalence with continuous semilinear Γ-spaces
A.65–A.66: descent of closed subschemes and of morphisms with separated target, including the graph criterion and its variety-only rational-point clause

sources.title: SGA 3, Exposé VIII, Groupes diagonalisables (Polo–Gille reedition)
sources.locator: Exposé VIII §1 (Bidualité), PDF pp. 1–7 of the 30-page exposé: Déf. 1.0–1.1, Thm. 1.2–1.3, Cor. 1.4–1.6 and the §1.7 effective-descent remark. Complete text of the listed pages read.

contents.name: VIII 1.1: G is diagonalizable if isomorphic to D_S(M)=Hom_{S-gr}(M_S,G_m) for a commutative group M
VIII 1.2–1.3: biduality for locally diagonalizable groups and the identification of D(M)(S′) with Hom(M,G_m(S′))
VIII 1.4–1.6: Hom_{S-gr}(M_S,N_S)≅Hom_{S-gr}(D(N),D(M)) with the finite-type/locally diagonalizable hypotheses, and the Isom form
VIII 1.7: effective descent of affine schemes, citing SGA 1 VIII 2.1
contents.reason: The packet does not import the SGA 1 affine-descent citation: effective finite-Galois Hopf descent is proved locally in lem-finite-galois-descent-for-multiplicative-hopf-algebras, and the affineness lemma descends its map with the published fpqc-submersiveness supplier instead.

sources.title: SGA 3, Exposé IX, Groupes de type multiplicatif : homomorphismes (Polo–Gille reedition)
sources.locator: Exposé IX §1, PDF pp. 1–3 (running pp. 31–33, original margins pp. 37–39): Déf. 1.1–1.4; §2.1(a) PDF p. 4 (running p. 34); §5.0–5.4 PDF pp. 18–20 (running pp. 48–50). Complete text of the listed pages read.

contents.name: IX 1.1: a group is of multiplicative type if it is locally diagonalizable for the fpqc topology; quasi-isotrivial variants
IX 1.3–1.4: the type M ≅ Hom_{k-gr}(G,G_m) of a multiplicative-type group at a point is independent of the diagonalizing extension
IX 2.1(a): a multiplicative-type group is faithfully flat and affine over its base
IX 3.1–3.4, IX 4.7, IX 5.0–5.3: nilpotent rigidity and schematic density machinery used to compare central homomorphisms
contents.reason: These general-base deformation and density results are not reproduced; the pair's field-level separable splitting is proved with the finite-subcoalgebra and interpolation argument, so no consumer needs the rigidity imports.

contents.name: IX Cor. 5.4: a central homomorphism of multiplicative-type groups descends uniquely under an effective universal epimorphism with geometrically connected fibres

sources.title: SGA 3, Exposé X, Caractérisation et classification des groupes de type multiplicatif (Polo–Gille reedition)
sources.locator: Exposé X §1, PDF pp. 1–4 (running pp. 63–66, original margins pp. 77–80): Prop. 1.1, Cor. 1.2, Rem. 1.5–1.6 and Prop. 1.4 with its proof. Complete text of the listed pages read.

contents.name: X Prop. 1.1: multiplicative-type groups split by a finite principal Γ-covering are anti-equivalent to Γ-modules

X Cor. 1.2: for a connected base with geometric point, isotrivial multiplicative-type groups correspond to π₁-modules with open stabilizers; over a field with a separable closure, finitely generated Galois modules
X 1.4 Prop. 1.4 and proof: every finite-type multiplicative-type group over any field splits over a finite separable extension, via the EGA finite-extension principle and IX 5.4
X 1.5–1.6: classification of isotrivial tori of relative dimension n by π₁→GL(n,Z), and non-isotrivial torus examples
contents.reason: The pair is field-level and does not build tori over a general connected base, so the relative isotrivial classification and its examples have no destination here.
